events_chronological: Years earlier the old woman Ottilie Crane tells Theo that every living creature on this earth dies alone.
On the second of the month Theo Lund is woken by a voice and sleepwalks out of the house onto a golf course.
A jet engine falls out of nowhere and destroys Theo's bedroom while he is outside.
In the restored timeline Theo stays in his bed laughing, and is killed when the engine comes through the roof.
Theo wakes on the green with a countdown of days, hours, minutes and seconds written on his arm by a figure in a hare costume who calls himself Vex.
The household is relocated while the roof is rebuilt, and no authority can account for where the engine came from.
Vex tells Theo the world will end in twenty-eight days.
Theo meets Marin Alder, a new girl seated next to him in a literature class, and asks her out.
On Vex's instruction Theo puts an axe through a water main to flood the school and buries the axe in the bronze mascot.
Theo's therapist Dr. Belding raises his medication and puts him under hypnosis.
The science teacher Nadeau lends Theo the old woman's book, The Shape of Hours.
Theo starts seeing liquid spears coming out of people's chests and leading them where they are going.
Theo humiliates the motivational speaker Vaughn Tice in front of the whole school, and the teacher Miss Hobbs is sacked over her syllabus.
Tice is exposed as the owner of a child pornography ring after Theo burns his house down.
Theo and Marin sleep together during a costume party while his parents are away.
Theo takes Marin to find Ottilie Crane, and the bullies Cutch and Ryle attack them at her house.
A car driven by Vex in his hare costume runs Marin down and kills her.
Theo shoots Vex through the eye with his father's revolver.
Theo carries Marin's body up the hill and watches a vortex open over his house.
Theo sends the jet engine back through the vortex to the night of the second, closing the tangent universe, and on the thirtieth Marin cycles past the house not knowing who died there.
nonlinear_category_reason: The captioned month runs forward, and both insertions are earlier - the old woman's line, and the death the month cancels, withheld until last.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs forward through twenty-eight captioned days, so most of its bullets sit in calendar order. The displacement that matters is the last one: told-order bullet 20 shows the boy dying in his bed on the first night of the story, withheld until after the film has shown the entire month that this death cancels. Told-order bullet 12 is a flashback to before the film's opening.
fabula_notes: The film's own logic makes a single clean chronology impossible - the engine that falls on the first night is sent there from the last, so an event is its own cause. The ordering here is by calendar date, which puts the death fourth even though the film establishes it last; ordering instead by the tangent universe's internal experience would place it after everything else. The old woman's remark predates the film and is reported rather than staged.
